analysis: The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md. Head hunks (lines 99-101 and 1371-1374) add a note that each provider test shard is routed through its own CI lane (test-provider-K, with a link to build.md#ci-runner-routing). They also describe routing checks that pin per-shard lanes, fallback, timeout and read-only permissions, and that keep release workflows on literal Blacksmith runners, with no contact to the real plane. I examined both supplied base units (the full file text). I found no runtime code, key handling, attestation, App Attest authorization, WebSocket contract, cache (T-041), add-on hold or fan helper change. This is developer documentation only, so it alters no controls in TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011, TB-012 or TB-013, and no threat-model assumption is invalidated. The CI routing behavior, the runner-routing plane and the routing scripts are outside the supplied evidence, so I could not verify the claims, such as read-only permissions or that release workflows stay on literal runners. That is a documentation accuracy question, not a demonstrated security regression. No findings. Integration passes need no cross-file follow-up from this unit, apart from the unverified CI-routing implementation if other files in the PR change workflows.
